description: Loosely, a 'lost position' signal: it fires mostly mid- to late-game when the side to move is lost, meaning every move loses to a forced opponent four (often a zugzwang where an opponent threat sits right above a landing cell) and the mover has little or no counterplay of their own. Lost positions where the mover also has several threat cells do not fire. Early in the game an opponent's open vertical three in columns 0-2 also fires it.
effect: None measurable: zeroing it in lost positions changes move probabilities by under 0.03. Forcing it to max in ordinary positions adds 0.02-0.08 to the column the model already prefers.
notes: Scores: p1 their threat at/above landing F1 0.10; p2 parity threats 0.09; p3 lost by depth-7 search 0.194; p4 poisoned column with no own threats 0.08; p5 lost by search and <=1 own threat cell 0.200 (P 0.17, R 0.24, AUROC 0.60, sim 0.00). All 14 band-9 positions checked are teacher-lost on every move, but many lost positions do not fire, and the activation is asymmetric (vertical threes fire in cols 0-2, not 3-6). It may be a mixture or a value-like direction. Synthesis reaches 9.47 (dev max 9.04).
